newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Ecuador's Bucaram says he escaped assassination.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's Bucaram says he escaped assassination.

text.p: Ousted Ecuadorean President Abdala Bucaram said on Monday he would have been assassinated if he had refused to abandon the presidential palace in Quito this month.

The eccentric former president, summarily deposed by Ecuador's Congress on Feb. 6 on grounds of "mental incompetence," views his forced departure as a "coup d'etat." He quietly left the ornate Carondelet presidential palace on Feb. 7 after riot police clashed with thousands of demonstrators in nearby streets who were threatening to take the palace by force.
The demonstrators were led by congressional leader Fabian Alarcon, who was sworn in as acting president last week.

"They wanted to drag me out of the palace dead and set me on fire," Bucaram told reporters at Bogota's El Dorado airport on arriving from Buenos Aires. "I had told my people that I wouldn't budge because I was the president and had to uphold the constitution," he added.

Bucaram, popularly known as "El Loco" (madman), has said repeatedly Congress had no constitutional right to revoke his mandate without at least giving him the right to defend himself in an impeachment trial. He held the top job for just six months but effectively gave up his fight to remain in office on Feb. 9 after the military, which proved itself to be the final arbiter of power in Ecuador, withdrew all support for his government.
His dismissal followed a massive two-day strike that shut down most of Ecuador to protest against draconian economic measures Bucaram had unveiled in late December and early January.
Bucaram was due to meet Colombian President Ernesto Samper behind closed doors at the presidential palace late on Monday. He was then scheduled to leave for Panama.

A senior Colombian official said Bucaram was essentially right in calling his ouster a coup since it appeared to have been backed by the military. The official, who spoke on condition he not be identified, said it was not immediately clear if Colombia would seek to cancel a $110 million loan Samper made to Bucaram for a highway construction project shortly after he took office.
